news.title: Too big to brake: why Bangladesh and Pakistan escaped the visa brake, and what comes next
news.summary_en: A High Court judgment shows that several key sending countries had a near miss in being included in the UK Home Office's study visa breaks. With fresh compliance requirements looming, universities have been left to manage the largest markets themselves – but could fresh changes be on the horizon? Spencer Withrington investigates.
news.author: Spencer Withrington

news.title: Grads face career readiness “disconnect” as skills take centre stage
news.summary_en: Stakeholders are warning that AI and other technologies are creating a skills "disconnect" in the job market, with today's graduates expected to enter the workforce with the same skill levels as someone who has already gained several years of work experience.
news.author: Beth Kennedy

news.title: Australian universities back new benchmark for education agents
news.summary_en: Six major Australian education providers have joined a new initiative aiming to put student feedback at the heart of how education agents are evaluated and provide stronger evidence of their contribution to international education.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: Proposed new OPT fee would decimate the international talent pipeline
news.summary_en: Zuzana Čeplá Wootson, deputy director of federal policy at the Presidents’ Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration, argues that proposed OPT fees would harm students, employers and US competitiveness.
news.author: Zuzana Čeplá Wootson

news.title: Three signals shaping Australian international education ahead of AIEC 2026
news.summary_en: From slowing student growth and tighter visa settings to the rise of transnational education, Australia's international education sector is entering a new phase. Ahead of AIEC 2026, The PIE looks at the shifts likely to shape conversations on the ground.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: Enroly: UK CAS issuance falls 24% as visa refusals jump 44%
news.summary_en: International student recruitment at UK universities has taken another hit, with CAS issuance down almost a quarter year-on-year and visa refusals climbing sharply, new Enroly data suggests.
news.author: Kim Martin
